definition: Mathematical linguistics is the application of mathematics to model phenomena and solve problems in general linguistics and theoretical linguistics.
details: Mathematical linguistics has a significant amount of overlap with computational linguistics.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. In plain words: Mathematical linguistics is the application of mathematics to model phenomena and solve problems in general linguistics and theoretical linguistics. Here is how it actually plays out: Mathematical linguistics has a significant amount of overlap with computational linguistics. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. That pattern-earned fluency is Mathematical linguistics.
